newsitem.title: ANGOLA: UNITA says its ex-soldiers to blame for unrest.
newsitem.headline: UNITA says its ex-soldiers to blame for unrest.

text.p: - Ex-UNITA soldiers are to blame for an attack in southwestern Angola that displaced up to 5,000 people, a top UNITA representative in Luanda said on Friday.

"The trouble in southern Benguela Province last week was caused by former UNITA soldiers," said Abel Chivukuvuku, a member of UNITA's peace process negotiating team in Luanda and a special adviser to party leader Jonas Savimbi.
But he said the attackers were not now controlled by UNITA (Union for the Total Independence of Angola) and that the attacks were in response to aggression by civil defence units.
Diplomats and aid workers say they believe the units are supported by the government, which UNITA fought for two decades until a 1994 peace deal, despite government denials.
Chivukuvuku criticised the government and the United Nations, which has some 7,000 peacekeepers in the country, for hesitancy in dealing with the civil defence units.
He said that the maverick soldiers were now a responsibility of the United Nations, under whose auspices they were demobilised over the last year.
Last weekend around 5,000 people fled villages to the city of Cubal after an attack they blamed on UNITA.
Aid workers in Angola say they are worried about the situation in the Cubal region because it could delay the further implementation of demobilisation, a crucial step in Angola's long peace process.

Although the 1994 peace accord has brought the longest period of peace since Angola was plunged into civil war after independence from Portugal in 1975, a formal end to hostilities and the establishment of a unity government are still under discussion.
